questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a cross-linked, thermosetting polymer?
questions.solution:
Bakelite is formed by the condensation reaction of phenol with formaldehyde. It is a highly cross-linked, thermosetting polymer which, once molded, cannot be remolded or reshaped by heating.

PVC, Polystyrene, and PTFE (Teflon) are examples of thermoplastic polymers, which can be repeatedly softened by heating and hardened by cooling.

Answer: Bakelite

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is fully Fluorinated polymer?
questions.solution:
Teflon is the commercial name for polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE).

The monomer of Teflon is tetrafluoroethylene, which has the chemical formula $CF_2=CF_2$.

Since all the hydrogen atoms in the ethylene monomer are replaced by fluorine atoms, Teflon is a fully fluorinated polymer.

PVC (polyvinyl chloride) contains chlorine and hydrogen, neoprene contains chlorine and hydrogen, and Buna-S is a hydrocarbon polymer containing only carbon and hydrogen.

Answer: Teflon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomers used for preparation of glyptal?
questions.solution:
Glyptal is a condensation polymer belonging to the class of polyesters.

It is synthesized by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) and phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid).

The polymerization reaction involves the elimination of water molecules to form ester linkages between the monomers.

Answer: Ethylene glycol and phthalic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to obtain shampoo bottles?
questions.solution:
High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is a tough, hard, and rigid polymer with high tensile strength and excellent chemical resistance. Due to these properties, it is widely used in the manufacture of household articles like buckets, dustbins, pipes, and various types of bottles, including shampoo bottles and milk jugs.

Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is typically used for flexible items like squeeze bottles and packaging films, while Polypropylene (PP) is used for ropes and toys, and Polystyrene (PS) is used for making thermocol and cabinet casings.

Answer: HDPE

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is obtained by condensation polymerization method?
questions.solution:
Polythene is an addition polymer formed by the repeated addition of ethene monomers.

Polyacrylonitrile is an addition polymer formed by the addition polymerization of acrylonitrile.

Teflon is an addition polymer formed by the addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethene.

Dacron (also known as terylene) is a condensation polymer formed by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid with the elimination of water molecules.

Answer: Dacron

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is obtained by condensation polymerisation method ?
questions.solution:
To determine which polymer is obtained by condensation polymerisation, let us analyze each option:

1. $[\,\text{CF}_2 - \text{CF}_2\,]_n$ is Teflon (Polytetrafluoroethylene). It is formed by the addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene.

2. $[\,\text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2\,]_n$ is Polythene. It is formed by the addition polymerisation of ethene.

3. $[\,\text{NH} - (\text{CH}_2)_5 - \text{CO}\,]_n$ is Nylon 6. It is synthesized by the ring-opening polymerisation of caprolactam. Since no small molecule is eliminated during the process, it is technically considered an addition polymerisation.

4. The polymer shown in the image is Nylon 6,6, which has the repeating unit $[\,-\text{CO}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-(\text{CH}_2)_6-\text{NH}-\,]_n$. It is formed by the condensation polymerisation of adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine, accompanied by the elimination of water molecules.

Therefore, Nylon 6,6 is the polymer obtained by the condensation polymerisation method.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is classified as branched chain polymer?
questions.solution:
Low density polythene (LDPE) is synthesized by free radical polymerization, which involves chain transfer reactions that lead to a highly branched structure.

High density polythene (HDPE) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) are linear polymers.

Melamine-formaldehyde resin is a cross-linked or network polymer.

Answer: Low density polythene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify thermosetting polymer from following.
questions.solution:
Thermosetting polymers are cross-linked or heavily branched molecules, which on heating undergo extensive cross-linking in moulds and become infusible. These cannot be reused.

Examples of thermosetting polymers include Bakelite, urea-formaldehyde resins, and melamine-formaldehyde resins.

Polystyrene is a thermoplastic polymer.

Buna-S is an elastomer.

Terylene is a fibre.

Answer: Ureaformaldehyde resin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify ureaformaldehyde resin from following polymers?
questions.solution:
Urea-formaldehyde resin is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction between urea (NH_2-CO-NH_2$) and formaldehyde (HCHO$).

The initial reaction involves the formation of methylol urea derivatives, which then undergo condensation with the elimination of water molecules to form a cross-linked polymer network.

The repeating unit of the urea-formaldehyde polymer chain is derived from linking the nitrogen atoms of urea with the methylene ($-CH_2-$) group from formaldehyde.

The repeating unit is $[-NH-CO-NH-CH_2-]_n$.

Let us analyze the other options:
Option (1) is polyacrylamide.
Option (2) is polystyrene.
Option (4) is nylon-6, which is polycaprolactam.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the use of HDPE ?
questions.solution:
High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is a tough, hard, and rigid polymer. It is widely used in the manufacture of buckets, dustbins, bottles (such as shampoo bottles), and pipes.

Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is highly branched and flexible, making it suitable for shopping bags, squeeze bottles, toys, and flexible pipes.

Therefore, HDPE is used to prepare shampoo bottles.

Answer: To prepare shampoo bottles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is a starting material used to obtain viscose rayon ?
questions.solution:
Viscose rayon is a semi-synthetic polymer. It is obtained by the chemical treatment of natural cellulose, which is typically sourced from wood pulp.

The cellulose is first dissolved in an alkaline solution of sodium hydroxide and then treated with carbon disulfide to form cellulose xanthate. This is further dissolved in dilute sodium hydroxide to form a viscous solution called viscose, which is then extruded into an acid bath to regenerate cellulose in the form of fine filaments known as viscose rayon.

Therefore, the starting material used to obtain viscose rayon is cellulose.

Answer: Cellulose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of LDP from following.
questions.solution:
Low Density Polyethylene (LDP) is widely used for the preparation of flexible pipes for agriculture, irrigation, domestic water line connections, and as insulation for electric cables.

High Density Polyethylene (HDP) is used for the manufacture of buckets, dustbins, and rigid pipes.

Teflon (Polytetrafluoroethylene) is used for making non-stick cookware.

Nylon 6 is used for making tyre cords, fabrics, and ropes.

Answer: Preparation of pipes for irrigation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is NOT obtained by addition polymerisation method?
questions.solution:
Teflon is an addition polymer of tetrafluoroethene.

Polyacrylonitrile is an addition polymer of acrylonitrile.

LDP (Low-density polyethylene) is an addition polymer of ethene.

PHBV (Poly $\beta$-hydroxybutyrate-co-$\beta$-hydroxyvalerate) is a condensation polymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid.

Answer: PHBV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a first stage in preparation of viscose rayon ?
questions.solution:
The preparation of viscose rayon involves several steps.

In the first stage, cellulose is treated with a concentrated solution of sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) to form alkali cellulose. The reaction is:
$\text{Cell}-\text{OH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Cell}-\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

In the subsequent stages, the alkali cellulose is reacted with carbon disulfide ($\text{CS}_2$) to form sodium cellulose xanthate, which is then dissolved in dilute $\text{NaOH}$ to form a viscous solution called viscose. Finally, it is extruded into an acid bath to regenerate cellulose fibers.

Therefore, the first stage is the reaction of cellulose with $\text{NaOH}$.

Answer: $\text{Cell} - \text{OH} + \text{NaOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the polymer used to prepare disposable cups and plates.
questions.solution:
Polystyrene is a synthetic aromatic hydrocarbon polymer made from the monomer styrene. It is widely used in the manufacture of disposable cups, plates, toys, radio and television cabinets, and as a wrapping material.

Polypropylene is used for ropes, toys, pipes, and fibres.

Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is used for making bottles and synthetic fibres.

High density polyethylene (HDPE) is used for buckets, dustbins, bottles, and pipes.

Answer: Polystyrene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymer is obtained by addition polymerization?
questions.solution:
Addition polymerization involves the repeated addition of monomer molecules possessing double or triple bonds to form a polymer, without the elimination of any small molecules.

Option (322647) represents Polyacrylonitrile (PAN), which is formed by the addition polymerization of acrylonitrile ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CN}$).

Option (322648) represents Nylon-6, which is a condensation polymer of caprolactam.

Option (322649) represents Terylene (Dacron), which is a condensation polymer of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

Option (322650) represents PHBV, which is a condensation polymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid.

Therefore, the polymer obtained by addition polymerization is Polyacrylonitrile.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to obtain articles like rain coats?
questions.solution:
Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is a widely used synthetic plastic polymer. It is water-resistant and durable, making it the primary material used in the manufacture of articles like raincoats, hand bags, vinyl flooring, and water pipes.

The monomer of PVC is vinyl chloride ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$). Upon polymerization, it forms PVC, which has the repeating unit $-\left[\text{CH}_2 - \underset{\text{Cl}}{\text{CH}}\right]_n-$.

Answer: $-\!\!\left[\text{CH}_2 - \underset{\text{Cl}}{\text{CH}}\right]\!\!-_n$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a homopolymer ?
questions.solution:
A homopolymer is a polymer which is formed from only one type of monomer.

Polyacrylonitrile is formed by the addition polymerization of a single monomer, acrylonitrile.

Buna-N is a copolymer formed from two different monomers, 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile.

Urea formaldehyde resin is a condensation copolymer formed from urea and formaldehyde.

Polycarbonate is a condensation copolymer typically formed from bisphenol A and phosgene.

Therefore, polyacrylonitrile is the only homopolymer among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Buna-S is prepared from
questions.solution:
Buna-S is a copolymer synthesized from $1,3$-butadiene and styrene in the presence of sodium as a catalyst.

The "Bu" stands for $1,3$-butadiene, "na" stands for sodium, and "S" stands for styrene.

The polymerization reaction involves the addition of $1,3$-butadiene and styrene molecules to form the elastomer Buna-S, which is also known as styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR).

Answer: 1, 3- butadiene and styrene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which polymer is commonly used in nonstick cookwares ?
questions.solution:
Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is chemically inert and highly resistant to heat. It has a very low coefficient of friction, which prevents food from sticking to the surface.

Therefore, Teflon is commonly used as a coating in nonstick cookware.

Answer: Teflon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the polymer used to prepare plastic bottles needed to store cooking oil.
questions.solution:
Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a strong, lightweight, and transparent synthetic resin belonging to the polyester family of polymers.

It provides an excellent barrier to oxygen and moisture, making it highly suitable for food packaging.

PET is widely blow-moulded into disposable plastic bottles used for storing cooking oil, mineral water, and carbonated beverages.

Answer: PET

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not a basis of classification of polymers ?
questions.solution:
Polymers are broadly classified on the basis of the following parameters:

1. Source (Natural, semi-synthetic, and synthetic polymers)
2. Structure (Linear, branched-chain, and cross-linked polymers)
3. Mode of polymerisation or method of preparation (Addition and condensation polymers)
4. Molecular forces (Elastomers, fibres, thermoplastics, and thermosetting polymers)

Polymers are not classified on the basis of the number of monomers. (Note: Based on the types of monomers, they are classified into homopolymers and copolymers, but not on the number of monomers).

Answer: Number of monomers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes develops cross-links in elastomer?
questions.solution:
Vulcanization is the chemical process of heating natural rubber with sulfur to improve its physical properties. During this process, sulfur forms cross-links between the polyisoprene chains of the elastomer, which makes the rubber harder, stronger, and more elastic.

Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to iron or steel to prevent rusting.

Polymerization is the process of forming a polymer from monomers.

Hydration is the addition of water molecules to a substance.

Answer: vulcanization

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT a polyester polymer ?
questions.solution:
Glyptal is a polyester polymer formed by the condensation of ethylene glycol and phthalic acid.

PHBV (Poly $\beta$-hydroxybutyrate-co-$\beta$-hydroxyvalerate) is a biodegradable aliphatic polyester.

Dacron (Terylene) is a polyester polymer formed by the condensation of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

Novolac is a linear condensation polymer of phenol and formaldehyde, which does not contain ester linkages. Therefore, it is not a polyester polymer.

Answer: Novolac

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomers used to prepare bakelite from the following.
questions.solution:
Bakelite is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction of phenol with formaldehyde in the presence of either an acid or a base catalyst.

The IUPAC name of formaldehyde is methanal.

Therefore, the monomers used to prepare bakelite are phenol and methanal.

Answer: phenol , methanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which properties from following is improved by vulcanization of rubber?
questions.solution:
Natural rubber becomes soft at high temperatures and brittle at low temperatures. It also shows high water absorption capacity, is soluble in non-polar solvents, and has low tensile strength.

To improve these physical properties, vulcanization is carried out by heating a mixture of raw rubber with sulfur and an appropriate additive. This process introduces sulfur cross-links between the polymer chains.

As a result of vulcanization, the rubber becomes more elastic, less plastic, insoluble in organic solvents, and its tensile strength is significantly improved.

Answer: Tensile strength

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following polymers has ester linkage?
questions.solution:
Dacron (also known as polyethylene terephthalate or PET) is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid. Since it is formed by the condensation of an alcohol and a carboxylic acid, it contains ester linkages ($-COO-$) and is classified as a polyester.

Orlon (polyacrylonitrile), Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene), and Neoprene (polychloroprene) are addition polymers and do not contain ester linkages.

Answer: Dacron

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is chain growth polymer?
questions.solution:
Chain growth polymers are formed by the repeated addition of monomer molecules possessing double or triple bonds, which is also known as addition polymerization.

Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is formed by the addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethene (CF_2=CF_2$). Thus, it is a chain growth polymer.

Nylon-6, Nylon-66, and Terylene are condensation polymers, which are formed by step growth polymerization.

Answer: Teflon$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the polymer obtained by addition polymerization method from following.
questions.solution:
Addition polymerization involves the repeated addition of monomer molecules possessing double or triple bonds to form a polymer without the elimination of any small molecules.

Polythene is formed by the addition polymerization of ethene (CH_2=CH_2$) molecules.

Nylon 6, Dacron, and Nylon 6,6 are formed by condensation polymerization, which involves the elimination of small molecules like water.

Answer: Polythene$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Name the catalyst used in the manufacture of HDPE polymer.
questions.solution:
High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is manufactured by the coordination polymerization of ethene using a Ziegler-Natta catalyst.

The Ziegler-Natta catalyst is a mixture of triethyl aluminum, $(C_2H_5)_3Al$, and titanium tetrachloride, $TiCl_4$.

Answer: Triethyl aluminum with titanium tetrachloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of polymer the natural rubber is?
questions.solution:
Natural rubber is an addition polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). It has weak intermolecular forces of attraction (van der Waals forces) between its polymer chains, which permit the polymer to be stretched. A few cross-links are introduced between the chains, which help the polymer retract to its original position after the force is released. Polymers with such elastic properties are classified as elastomers.

Therefore, natural rubber is an elastomer.

Answer: Elastomer

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomer used to prepare orlon.
questions.solution:
Orlon is the trade name for polyacrylonitrile (PAN).

It is an addition polymer formed by the polymerisation of acrylonitrile.

The chemical reaction is:

$n CH_2=CH-CN \xrightarrow{\text{Polymerisation}} [-CH_2-CH(CN)-]_n$

Thus, the monomer used to prepare orlon is acrylonitrile.

Answer: acrylonitrile

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the monomer of Teflon polymer?
questions.solution:
Teflon is the commercial name for polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE).

It is an addition polymer formed by the polymerization of tetrafluoroethylene.

The chemical formula of the monomer tetrafluoroethylene is $\text{CF}_2 = \text{CF}_2$.

Answer: $\text{CF}_2 = \text{CF}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Buna - S is an example of ,
questions.solution:
Buna-S is a synthetic rubber formed by the copolymerization of 1,3-butadiene and styrene.

Since it is a rubber, it possesses elastic properties and is classified as an elastomer.

The intermolecular forces in elastomers are weak van der Waals forces, which allow the polymer chains to be stretched.

Answer: elastomer

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following polymers is also called as dacron?
questions.solution:
Dacron is the trade name for the polymer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) in the United States, while in the United Kingdom, it is commonly known as Terylene.

It is a polyester made by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

Therefore, Terylene is also called Dacron.

Answer: Terylene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds are used to obtain terylene polymer?
questions.solution:
Terylene, also known as Dacron, is a polyester.

It is prepared by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

The IUPAC name of ethylene glycol is ethane-1,2-diol.

The IUPAC name of terephthalic acid is benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

Therefore, the monomers used to obtain terylene are ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

Answer: Ethane-1,2-diol and Benzene-1, 4 dicarboxylic acid
questions.question: Which of the following compounds are used to obtain terylene polymer?
questions.explanation:
Terylene, also known as Dacron, is a polyester.

It is prepared by the condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid.

The IUPAC name of ethylene glycol is ethane-1,2-diol.

The IUPAC name of terephthalic acid is benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

Therefore, the monomers used to obtain terylene are ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid.

Answer: Ethane-1,2-diol and Benzene-1, 4 dicarboxylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify cross linked polymer from following.
questions.solution:
The question requires identifying which polymer has a cross-linked structure from the given options.

High density polythene (HDPE) is a linear polymer with high crystallinity and thermoplastic behavior, lacking cross-links.

Low density polythene (LDPE) is highly branched but remains thermoplastic without cross-linking.

Melamine refers to melamine-formaldehyde resin, a thermosetting polymer characterized by extensive cross-linking that forms a rigid, three-dimensional network structure, rendering it infusible upon heating.

PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) is a linear thermoplastic polymer without cross-links.

Melamine is the cross-linked polymer among the options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the name of monomer used in the formation of a polymer
?
questions.solution:
The repeating unit $\text{–CH}_2\text{–C(CH}_3)\text{=CH–CH}_2\text{–}$ indicates 1,4-addition polymerization of a conjugated diene.

Reversing the polymerization by breaking the terminal single bonds and reforming the conjugated system yields the monomer $\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3)\text{–CH=CH}_2$, known as isoprene.

Comparing with options: tetrafluoroethylene ($\text{CF}_2\text{=CF}_2$) forms Teflon; acrylonitrile ($\text{CH}_2\text{=CH–CN}$) forms polyacrylonitrile; caprolactam undergoes ring-opening polymerization to form Nylon-6. Only isoprene corresponds to the given structure.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used as surgical suture?
questions.solution:
Surgical sutures require materials with high tensile strength, flexibility, and biocompatibility. Among the given polymers, both polyamides (Nylon 6 and Nylon 6,6) are used for non-absorbable sutures.
Nylon 6 in particular is widely employed due to its optimal balance of strength and handling characteristics, with common examples including Ethilon and Dermalon sutures.

High-density polyethylene and polyacrylonitrile lack the necessary properties for this medical application.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a thermosetting polymer?
questions.solution:
Thermosetting polymers undergo irreversible cross-linking upon heating, forming rigid, infusible structures. Analyzing the options:

Buna-S is a synthetic rubber copolymer exhibiting thermoplastic behavior. Dacron (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyvinyls like PVC are also thermoplastic polymers.

Bakelite, a phenol-formaldehyde resin, forms extensive cross-links during curing and cannot be reshaped after polymerization, confirming its thermosetting nature.

The thermosetting polymer is therefore $\boxed{D}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomers used in preparation of dacron.
questions.solution:
Dacron (Terylene) is a polyester formed by condensation polymerization between a dicarboxylic acid and a diol. The specific monomers are ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) and terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid).

Option A represents phenol and formaldehyde, monomers for Bakelite. Option B contains 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile, monomers for Buna-N rubber. Option D includes acrylonitrile and phenol, unrelated to polyester synthesis.

Option C contains the correct monomers: $\mathrm{HO}(\mathrm{CH}_2)_2\mathrm{OH}$ (ethylene glycol) and $\mathrm{HO}\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_4\mathrm{C}(=\mathrm{O})\mathrm{OH}$ (terephthalic acid).

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to obtain surgical sutures?
questions.solution:
Surgical sutures require materials with high tensile strength, flexibility, and biocompatibility. Among common polymers, Nylon 6 (polyamide) possesses these properties and is widely employed as a non-absorbable suture material.

Terylene (polyethylene terephthalate) is primarily used in textiles and packaging, while neoprene (polychloroprene) serves industrial applications requiring chemical resistance. Though Nylon 6,6 shares some characteristics, Nylon 6 remains the standard choice due to its specific mechanical and biological performance.

The polymer used for surgical sutures is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers does NOT contain either —COO— or —CO—NH— linkage in it?
questions.solution:
To identify which polymer lacks both ester (—COO—) and amide (—CO—NH—) linkages, examine the structural composition of each:

Perspex (polymethyl methacrylate) contains ester linkages from its methyl methacrylate monomer $\mathrm{CH_2=C(CH_3)COOCH_3}$, forming $[—\mathrm{CH_2—C(CH_3)(COOCH_3)—}]_n$.

Polyacrylamide includes amide linkages derived from acrylamide $\mathrm{CH_2=CHCONH_2}$, yielding $[—\mathrm{CH_2—CH(CONH_2)—}]_n$.

Glyptal, a polyester resin synthesized from phthalic acid and glycerol, inherently contains ester linkages.

Thermocol (polystyrene) polymerizes from styrene $\mathrm{C_6 H_5CH=CH_2}$ via addition polymerization, resulting in $[—\mathrm{CH(C_6 H_5)—CH_2—}]_n$ with a hydrocarbon backbone and phenyl substituents, devoid of ester or amide functional groups.

Thus, Thermocol is the polymer without —COO— or —CO—NH— linkages.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the compounds used to obtain nylon salt?
questions.solution:
Nylon 6,6 salt forms through the reaction between adipic acid ($\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2)4-COOH}$) and hexamethylenediamine ($\mathrm{H2N-(CH_2)6-NH_2}$). This salt undergoes condensation polymerization to yield the final polyamide.

Hydrogen bonding stabilizes the crystal lattice in nylon 6,6, contributing to its high melting point and mechanical strength.

Option A employs a monoamine, which cannot form the required repeating unit. Option B uses terephthalic acid, which produces polyesters rather than nylons. Option D involves a hydroxy acid, resulting in a different polymer structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used as wool substitute?
questions.solution:
Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) serves as a wool substitute due to its similar tactile properties: warmth, soft texture, and resistance to moths and chemicals. Marketed under names like Orlon and Acrilan, it appears in sweaters, blankets, and carpets.

Glyptal is a polyester resin for paints, Terylene a durable polyester fiber for fabrics, and Neoprene a synthetic rubber for industrial uses. None exhibit wool-like characteristics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following house hold plastic material is used to prepare drinking straws ?
questions.solution:
PVC is a rigid plastic used primarily for construction materials and insulation, not typically for drinking straws due to its inflexibility.

LDPE lacks sufficient structural rigidity for straw applications despite its flexibility.

PS is brittle and not ideal for the bending required in typical straw usage.

PP possesses the optimal combination of flexibility, chemical resistance, and durability required for drinking straws, making it the standard material choice.

The correct identification is $\boxed{D}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomers used in preparation of Nylon 2- nylon 6
options: $\beta$ - hydroxy butyric acid and $\beta$ - hydroxy valeric acid
questions.solution:
Nylon 2-Nylon 6 is a biodegradable polyamide formed via condensation polymerization of two amino acids: glycine and $\epsilon$-aminocaproic acid.

Analyzing the options:
Option A corresponds correctly to these monomers.
Option B represents $\beta$-hydroxybutyric acid and $\beta$-hydroxyvaleric acid, monomers of polyester PHBV.
Option C consists of polyester monomers ethylene glycol and phthalic acid.
Option D comprises addition polymer monomers acrylamide and vinyl chloride.

$\boxed{A}$ is correct, as only pair A forms the specified polyamide structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify polyamide polymer from following.
questions.solution:
Polyamide identification: A polyamide contains repeating amide linkages ($-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}^-$).

SBR is a rubber copolymer without amide groups. Melamine formaldehyde contains $\mathrm{C-N}$ bonds but is an amino resin rather than a polyamide. Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin lacking amide linkages.

Nylon 6,6 forms through condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, producing characteristic amide bonds. This makes it the polyamide among the options.

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to obtain rubber belts?
questions.solution:
The analysis of polymer suitability indicates Buna-N is uniquely appropriate for rubber belt production.

Buna-N (Nitrile Butadiene Rubber) is a synthetic copolymer of acrylonitrile and butadiene, offering exceptional resistance to oils, fuels, and chemicals. This property profile makes it the preferred material for industrial belts operating in demanding environments, particularly conveyor and drive belts requiring oil resistance.

Other polymers lack the necessary elastomeric properties: Perspex (PMMA) is a rigid transparent thermoplastic, PVC serves primarily as a versatile plastic for construction and insulation, and polycarbonate provides impact resistance for protective applications. None exhibit the flexible, durable characteristics required for rubber belts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a polyester fibre?
questions.solution:
Identifying the polyester fiber: The ester functional group defines polyesters, which are polymers containing repeating ester units in their main chain.

Option A, PHBV (poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate)), is a biodegradable copolymer formed from hydroxy acids. Its structure contains ester linkages, confirming it as a polyester.

Option B, urea formaldehyde, is an amino resin produced from urea and formaldehyde condensation, lacking ester bonds.
Option C, thermocol (expanded polystyrene), is a vinyl polymer derived from styrene monomer.
Option D, polyacrylonitrile, is an acrylic polymer with nitrile functional groups.

Only PHBV possesses the characteristic ester linkages of polyesters.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is biodegradable?
questions.solution:
Nylon 2-nylon 6 is the biodegradable polymer among the options.

While nylon 6 and nylon 6,6 are synthetic polyamides with poor biodegradability, and high-density polyethylene exhibits high resistance to degradation, nylon 2-nylon 6 is a copolymer of glycine and aminocaproic acid.

The amide linkages derived from these amino acids render it susceptible to enzymatic hydrolysis, enabling biodegradation.

The biodegradable polymer is therefore $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to obtain oil seals?
questions.solution:
Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene, PTFE) is the correct material for oil seals due to its combination of chemical inertness, thermal stability, and low friction coefficient. As a synthetic fluoropolymer, it demonstrates exceptional resistance to oils, chemicals, and extreme temperatures, which are critical properties for seal integrity and durability.

While Dacron (a polyester), Nylon 6 (a polyamide), and low-density polyethylene serve various applications, none provide the superior performance required for oil seals as effectively as Teflon.

The final answer is $\boxed{A}$.

Option A yields Nylon 6,6, option B produces Dacron, and option D forms Bakelite.

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

questions.q: Identify a monomer used in preparation of neoprene.

A) 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene (isoprene): monomer for natural rubber
B) 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene (chloroprene): monomer for neoprene
C) Melamine: monomer for melamine-formaldehyde resin
D) 1,3-butadiene: monomer for Buna-S and Buna-N rubbers

The monomer for neoprene is thus 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers contains $-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}-$ linkage ?
questions.solution:
The $\mathrm{-CO-NH-}$ linkage corresponds to an amide functional group found in polyamides and related polymers.

Glyptal is a polyester formed from phthalic acid and ethylene glycol, containing ester linkages ($\mathrm{-COO-}$) but no amide groups.

Thermocol (expanded polystyrene) is an addition polymer of styrene, lacking heteroatom functional groups.

Buna-N is a copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile; though acrylonitrile contains a nitrile group ($\mathrm{-CN}$), polymerization yields carbon-carbon backbone chains without amide linkages.

Urea-formaldehyde resin forms via condensation polymerization between urea ($\mathrm{H2N-CO-NH_2}$) and formaldehyde. The polymer network retains the amide linkage from urea while incorporating methylene bridges between nitrogen atoms.

Only urea-formaldehyde resin contains the $\mathrm{-CO-NH-}$ linkage.

questions.q: Identify the monomer of natural rubber.
questions.solution:
Natural rubber is a polymer whose monomer unit is isoprene, or 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene. Polymerization occurs via a cis-1,4 addition to form cis-1,4-polyisoprene.

Option analysis:
A) Isoprene is the correct monomer.
B) Polyacrylonitrile is a polymer, not a monomer.
C) Chloroprene is the monomer for neoprene, a synthetic rubber.
D) Tetrafluoroethylene is the monomer for Teflon.

Only A correctly identifies the monomer of natural rubber.

questions.q: Which from following polymers is used to prepare shoe soles?
questions.solution:
Buna-N is the correct choice due to its favorable properties for shoe sole manufacturing. As a copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile, it offers high resistance to oils, fuels, and chemicals, alongside good abrasion resistance and elasticity.

By contrast, polyacrylamide is employed in water treatment and electrophoresis, Perspex serves as a transparent glass substitute, and Glyptal functions as a resin in paints and varnishes—none possess the durability or chemical resistance required for shoe soles.

Thus, Buna-N is uniquely suited for this application.

As a thermosetting polymer, its primary application is in the manufacture of paints and lacquers due to its superior adhesive and flexible properties, though it is also used in binding materials and certain molding compounds.

Among the given choices:

Option A involves electrophoresis gels, typically composed of agarose or polyacrylamide.
Option B corresponds to paints, aligning with glyptal's predominant use.
Option C pertains to decorative laminates, commonly utilizing melamine-formaldehyde or phenolic resins.
Option D refers to food-grade containers, usually made from polyethylene, polypropylene, or PET.

The correct option is $\boxed{B}$.

Analyzing each polymer:

Buna-S is synthesized from 1,3-butadiene and styrene, making it a copolymer.

Polyacrylonitrile is derived solely from acrylonitrile, classifying it as a homopolymer.

Polypropene results from polymerization of propene, also a homopolymer.

Nylon 6,6 is formed through condensation of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, qualifying as a copolymer.

Thus, Buna-S and Nylon 6,6 are copolymers.

The correct options are A and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a thermosetting polymer ?
questions.solution:
Polymers are classified by thermal behavior into thermoplastics and thermosetting polymers. Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be remolded, as seen in polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polystyrene, and nylon 6,6. Thermosetting polymers undergo irreversible hardening upon heating and cannot be remolded; examples include urea-formaldehyde resin, bakelite, and melamine-formaldehyde resin.

Among the options: $A$, $B$, and $D$ are thermoplastics, while $C$ (urea-formaldehyde) is thermosetting.

The thermosetting polymer is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.q: Identify the monomer used in preparation of polyacrylonitrile?
questions.solution:
The polymer polyacrylonitrile (PAN) derives its name directly from its monomer acrylonitrile, an addition polymer formed through vinyl polymerization.

Acrylonitrile has the structure $\mathrm{H_2C=CH-CN}$, featuring a vinyl group and nitrile functionality that polymerizes via the carbon-carbon double bond.

Evaluating the options:

$\mathrm{H_2C=C(CH_3)-CH=CH_2}$ (isoprene) produces polyisoprene

$\mathrm{F_2C=CF_2}$ (tetrafluoroethylene) yields polytetrafluoroethylene

$\mathrm{H_2C=CH-CN}$ (acrylonitrile) forms polyacrylonitrile

$\mathrm{H_2C=CH-CH=CH_2}$ (1,3-butadiene) generates polybutadiene

Only acrylonitrile corresponds to the specified polymer, confirming option C as correct.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.q: Which from following polymers is obtained by condensation polymerisation method?
questions.solution:
Condensation polymerization produces polymers through monomer reactions that eliminate small molecules such as water, methanol, or hydrogen chloride as byproducts.

Polythene results from addition polymerization of ethylene monomers, with no small molecules eliminated.

Nylon 6,6 forms via condensation polymerization between hexamethylenediamine $\mathrm{H_2 N-(CH_2 )_6 -NH_2 }$ and adipic acid $\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2 )_4 -COOH}$, with water molecules eliminated during amide bond formation.

Polyacrylonitrile and Teflon both derive from addition polymerization of acrylonitrile and tetrafluoroethylene respectively, neither process eliminating small molecules.

The condensation polymerization product is Nylon 6,6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following polymers is classified as fibre?
questions.solution:
Polymers are classified based on intermolecular forces and physical properties:

Fibres exhibit high tensile strength and modulus due to strong intermolecular forces like hydrogen bonding or dipole–dipole interactions, enabling dense chain packing.

$\text{Nylon 6,6}$ is a polyamide with strong hydrogen bonding between chains, providing the characteristic tensile strength and elasticity required for fibres.

$\text{Urea formaldehyde resin}$ is a rigid thermosetting plastic, $\text{polystyrene}$ a thermoplastic, and $\text{neoprene}$ an elastomer—none exhibit the structural properties of fibres.

Thus, $\text{Nylon 6,6}$ is correctly classified as a fibre.

The final answer is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.q: Which from following polymers needs peroxide as initiator for preparation?

Analysis of polymer synthesis mechanisms:

Nylon 6,6 is produced through condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, requiring no radical initiator.

Polyacrylonitrile undergoes addition polymerization of acrylonitrile ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CN}$) via free radical mechanism, typically initiated by peroxides.

Terylene forms through condensation polymerization of terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol, eliminating the need for radical initiators.

Bakelite results from condensation polymerization of phenol and formaldehyde, also not requiring peroxide initiation.

Conclusion: Only polyacrylonitrile utilizes peroxide initiators in its preparation.

questions.q: Which from following polymers is obtained by addition polymerisation method?
questions.solution:

Nylon 6 undergoes ring-opening polymerization, a subtype of condensation polymerization involving molecular elimination.

Terylene is a polyester formed via condensation polymerization of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid with water elimination.

Nylon 6,6 is a polyamide synthesized through condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, also eliminating water.

Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is produced by addition polymerization of tetrafluoroethene ($\mathrm{CF2=CF2}$), where all monomer atoms are incorporated into the polymer without any byproducts.

The polymer formed by addition polymerization is Teflon.

questions.q: Which among the following statements about terpenes is NOT true?
options: Terpenes include vitamin A, E and $\mathrm{K}$
questions.solution:
Terpenes are hydrocarbons that are classified by the number of isoprene units (C5H8), with the most common being mono-, sesqui-, and di-terpenes (C10, C15, and C20, respectively).
Terpenes are highly aromatic compounds that determine the smell of many plants and herbs, such as rosemary and lavender, as well as some animals. Manufacturers use isolated terpenes to create the flavors and scents of many everyday products, such as perfumes, body products, and even foods.
The side chains of Vitamin A, E, K, squalene (unsaturated hydrocarbon found in shark, humans) are all constituents of terpenes.
Terpenes are important constituents of essential oils, having a chemical structure consisting of repeated isoprene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{5} \mathrm{H}_{8}\right)$ units. They are classified into monoterpenes $\left(C_{10}\right)$, sesquiterpenes $\left(C_{15}\right)$, and diterpenes $\left(C_{20}\right)$ based on whether they are made up of two, three, or four isoprene units respectively.
